title: Studying with Eddie Barefield and Big Nick Nicholas
summary: She studied with Eddie Barefield and Big Nick Nicholas, who insisted on learning lyrics for color; they discuss Nicholas's Jazzmobile work.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Yeah. And I’m trying to think — I know one of the big teachers I had, but this was a little bit later — I’m trying to think who I studied with in Boston because I know there was someone — maybe I’ll think of that later. But I went to Eddie Barefield in New York, he was wonderful. And then I went to Big Nick Nicholas. And I went to him because of the

colors he got out of the tenor, you know, the beautiful nuances and color, and especially when he played like Strayhorn tunes, and I wanted to get an idea about that. And it was very interesting, the lessons with him, because he was very insistent on learning the lyrics to songs before you played them. And I think that’s where the color came from — understanding the meaning of the song in terms of the lyrics.
Boy, he did a lot of session playing I believe — rock & roll and just about everything that came along.

Big Nick was amazing that way, yeah. I mean you can hear him in big bands. And when he would do the Jazzmobile he would take any popular song like “Hot Hot Hot” or something like that, and make it into a beautiful jazz tune, and he was always sort of dancing while he played and then he’d sing.
That’s right. He was just written up in the New York Times a few months ago. Because I think he passed away not that long ago.
No it’s been quite a long time.
Okay. Well it must have been an anniversary or something.
